Design map

Target population

English-fluent Prolific members with approval rate above 90%; broader target population NR.
a) fluency in English and b) approval rate above 90%PDF page 7 · Materials and Methods, RTs and Experimental Design Requirements

The common Prolific eligibility screen required English fluency and an approval rate above 90%.

Eligibility criteria

English fluency; Prolific approval rate >90%; attention check and captcha before redirection. Design-specific ex-post eligibility/exclusion rules NR.
a) fluency in English and b) approval rate above 90%PDF page 7 · Materials and Methods, RTs and Experimental Design Requirements

The common Prolific eligibility screen required English fluency and an approval rate above 90%.

only include ‘completed observations’PDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches

Focal analyses include valid completion-code observations and exclude later observations from repeat participants.

Recruitment procedure

One common Prolific study recruited by project coordinators.
project coordinators recruited participants ... via ProlificPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 1

Participants were recruited through one common Prolific study by the project coordinators.

Field dates and setting

Online via Prolific, January 17–28, 2022, ten weekday slots starting 2 pm GMT, plus a final continuation after slot ten.
January 17 to January 28, 2022PDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 4

Main data collection occurred online across ten weekday time slots; collection continued after the tenth slot to exceed 18,000 completions.

Number recruited and analyzed

NR for this design. Article reports 18,123 completed overall and about 400 per design; starts/randomized counts per design are not reported.
18,123 completed observations (about 400 per design)PDF page 2 · Introduction/results overview

The article gives the pooled completed count and only an approximate per-design count, not an exact count for each design.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Two arms: competition and control.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Unit of randomization

Four-participant batch assigned to one design-by-condition cell.
randomly redirected ... in batches of four participantsPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Batches of four participants, rather than single participants, were redirected to design-by-condition cells.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

Restricted balanced cycles: each sequence of 90 four-person batches assigns one batch to each of 45×2 cells; numerical marginal probabilities are implied but not stated. No stratification statement.
one batch per treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Within each cycle of 90 batches, one four-person batch was randomly allocated to each of the 90 design-by-condition cells.

Exact treatment and comparator

NR; only the generic labels competition and control are in the main article.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Outcome definitions and timing

NR for this design; main article states only that teams prespecified a moral-behavior measure.
measure of moral behaviorPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, RT recruitment, second step

Each team defined its own moral-behavior outcome; the main article does not enumerate all definitions.

Estimand

Competition-versus-control effect on the design's moral-behavior outcome, standardized as Cohen's d.
effect of competition on moral behaviorPDF page 2 · Results, Meta-Analytic Effect Size

The target per-design contrast is competition versus control on moral behavior, standardized to Cohen's d for synthesis.

Estimator or statistical model

Approach A: team-preferred OLS of moral behavior on competition indicator, then Cohen's d conversion; team-specific specification and conversion procedure NR. Approach B: adapted standardized OLS, adaptations NR in main article.
ordinary least squares regression ... moral behavior ... indicator variable for the competition treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches A

Approach A required participant-level OLS of moral behavior on a competition indicator, but team-specific specifications are outside the main article.

with some adaptations as described further in SI AppendixPDF page 9 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches B

Approach B is said to adapt the OLS model, but those adaptations are not in the main article.

Analysis unit

Participant/participant observation.
ordinary least squares regression ... moral behavior ... indicator variable for the competition treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches A

Approach A required participant-level OLS of moral behavior on a competition indicator, but team-specific specifications are outside the main article.

18,123 completed observations (about 400 per design)PDF page 2 · Introduction/results overview

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Two arms: competition and control.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Unit of randomization

Four-participant batch assigned to one design-by-condition cell.
randomly redirected ... in batches of four participantsPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Batches of four participants, rather than single participants, were redirected to design-by-condition cells.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

Restricted balanced cycles: each sequence of 90 four-person batches assigns one batch to each of 45×2 cells; numerical marginal probabilities are implied but not stated. No stratification statement.
one batch per treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Within each cycle of 90 batches, one four-person batch was randomly allocated to each of the 90 design-by-condition cells.

Exact treatment and comparator

NR; only the generic labels competition and control are in the main article.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Outcome definitions and timing

NR for this design; main article states only that teams prespecified a moral-behavior measure.
measure of moral behaviorPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, RT recruitment, second step

Each team defined its own moral-behavior outcome; the main article does not enumerate all definitions.

Estimand

Competition-versus-control effect on the design's moral-behavior outcome, standardized as Cohen's d.
effect of competition on moral behaviorPDF page 2 · Results, Meta-Analytic Effect Size

The target per-design contrast is competition versus control on moral behavior, standardized to Cohen's d for synthesis.

Estimator or statistical model

Approach A: team-preferred OLS of moral behavior on competition indicator, then Cohen's d conversion; team-specific specification and conversion procedure NR. Approach B: adapted standardized OLS, adaptations NR in main article.
ordinary least squares regression ... moral behavior ... indicator variable for the competition treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches A

Approach A required participant-level OLS of moral behavior on a competition indicator, but team-specific specifications are outside the main article.

with some adaptations as described further in SI AppendixPDF page 9 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches B

Approach B is said to adapt the OLS model, but those adaptations are not in the main article.

Main data collection occurred online across ten weekday time slots; collection continued after the tenth slot to exceed 18,000 completions.

Number recruited and analyzed

NR for this design. Article reports 18,123 completed overall and about 400 per design; starts/randomized counts per design are not reported.
18,123 completed observations (about 400 per design)PDF page 2 · Introduction/results overview

The article gives the pooled completed count and only an approximate per-design count, not an exact count for each design.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Two arms: competition and control.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Unit of randomization

Four-participant batch assigned to one design-by-condition cell.
randomly redirected ... in batches of four participantsPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Batches of four participants, rather than single participants, were redirected to design-by-condition cells.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

Restricted balanced cycles: each sequence of 90 four-person batches assigns one batch to each of 45×2 cells; numerical marginal probabilities are implied but not stated. No stratification statement.
one batch per treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Within each cycle of 90 batches, one four-person batch was randomly allocated to each of the 90 design-by-condition cells.

Exact treatment and comparator

NR; only the generic labels competition and control are in the main article.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Outcome definitions and timing

NR for this design; main article states only that teams prespecified a moral-behavior measure.
measure of moral behaviorPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, RT recruitment, second step

Each team defined its own moral-behavior outcome; the main article does not enumerate all definitions.

Estimand

Competition-versus-control effect on the design's moral-behavior outcome, standardized as Cohen's d.
effect of competition on moral behaviorPDF page 2 · Results, Meta-Analytic Effect Size

The target per-design contrast is competition versus control on moral behavior, standardized to Cohen's d for synthesis.

Estimator or statistical model

Approach A: team-preferred OLS of moral behavior on competition indicator, then Cohen's d conversion; team-specific specification and conversion procedure NR. Approach B: adapted standardized OLS, adaptations NR in main article.
ordinary least squares regression ... moral behavior ... indicator variable for the competition treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches A

Approach A required participant-level OLS of moral behavior on a competition indicator, but team-specific specifications are outside the main article.

with some adaptations as described further in SI AppendixPDF page 9 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches B

Approach B is said to adapt the OLS model, but those adaptations are not in the main article.

Participant/participant observation.
ordinary least squares regression ... moral behavior ... indicator variable for the competition treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches A

Approach A required participant-level OLS of moral behavior on a competition indicator, but team-specific specifications are outside the main article.

Main data collection occurred online across ten weekday time slots; collection continued after the tenth slot to exceed 18,000 completions.

Number recruited and analyzed

NR for this design. Article reports 18,123 completed overall and about 400 per design; starts/randomized counts per design are not reported.
18,123 completed observations (about 400 per design)PDF page 2 · Introduction/results overview

The article gives the pooled completed count and only an approximate per-design count, not an exact count for each design.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Two arms: competition and control.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Unit of randomization

Four-participant batch assigned to one design-by-condition cell.
randomly redirected ... in batches of four participantsPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Batches of four participants, rather than single participants, were redirected to design-by-condition cells.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

Restricted balanced cycles: each sequence of 90 four-person batches assigns one batch to each of 45×2 cells; numerical marginal probabilities are implied but not stated. No stratification statement.
one batch per treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Within each cycle of 90 batches, one four-person batch was randomly allocated to each of the 90 design-by-condition cells.

Exact treatment and comparator

NR; only the generic labels competition and control are in the main article.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Outcome definitions and timing

NR for this design; main article states only that teams prespecified a moral-behavior measure.
measure of moral behaviorPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, RT recruitment, second step

Each team defined its own moral-behavior outcome; the main article does not enumerate all definitions.

Estimand

Competition-versus-control effect on the design's moral-behavior outcome, standardized as Cohen's d.
effect of competition on moral behaviorPDF page 2 · Results, Meta-Analytic Effect Size

The target per-design contrast is competition versus control on moral behavior, standardized to Cohen's d for synthesis.

Estimator or statistical model

Approach A: team-preferred OLS of moral behavior on competition indicator, then Cohen's d conversion; team-specific specification and conversion procedure NR. Approach B: adapted standardized OLS, adaptations NR in main article.
ordinary least squares regression ... moral behavior ... indicator variable for the competition treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches A

Approach A required participant-level OLS of moral behavior on a competition indicator, but team-specific specifications are outside the main article.

with some adaptations as described further in SI AppendixPDF page 9 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches B

Approach B is said to adapt the OLS model, but those adaptations are not in the main article.

Participant/participant observation.
ordinary least squares regression ... moral behavior ... indicator variable for the competition treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Analytic Approaches A

Approach A required participant-level OLS of moral behavior on a competition indicator, but team-specific specifications are outside the main article.

Field dates and setting

Online via Prolific, January 17–28, 2022, ten weekday slots starting 2 pm GMT, plus a final continuation after slot ten.
January 17 to January 28, 2022PDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 4

Main data collection occurred online across ten weekday time slots; collection continued after the tenth slot to exceed 18,000 completions.

Number recruited and analyzed

NR for this design. Article reports 18,123 completed overall and about 400 per design; starts/randomized counts per design are not reported.
18,123 completed observations (about 400 per design)PDF page 2 · Introduction/results overview

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Two arms: competition and control.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Unit of randomization

Four-participant batch assigned to one design-by-condition cell.
randomly redirected ... in batches of four participantsPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Batches of four participants, rather than single participants, were redirected to design-by-condition cells.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

Restricted balanced cycles: each sequence of 90 four-person batches assigns one batch to each of 45×2 cells; numerical marginal probabilities are implied but not stated. No stratification statement.
one batch per treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Within each cycle of 90 batches, one four-person batch was randomly allocated to each of the 90 design-by-condition cells.

Exact treatment and comparator

Stage 1 groups of four encode words for 5 minutes; competition gives symbolic medals by performance rank, whereas control gives no performance or rank feedback.
average ‘transfer’ to other playersPDF page 4 · Moderating Effect of Common Design Choices, BDQ29 example

The article specifies group size, five-minute task, symbolic-rank treatment, no-feedback control, transfer range/cost, and average-transfer outcome.

Outcome definitions and timing

In stage 2, each participant can increase or decrease each other member's 100-Taler endowment by up to 30 Taler at a one-Taler cost; average transfer is the moral-behavior measure.
average ‘transfer’ to other playersPDF page 4 · Moderating Effect of Common Design Choices, BDQ29 example

The article specifies group size, five-minute task, symbolic-rank treatment, no-feedback control, transfer range/cost, and average-transfer outcome.

effect of competition on moral behaviorPDF page 2 · Results, Meta-Analytic Effect Size

Approach A: team-preferred OLS of moral behavior on competition indicator, then Cohen's d conversion; team-specific specification and conversion procedure NR. Approach B: adapted standardized OLS, adaptations NR in main article.

project coordinators recruited participants ... via ProlificPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 1

Field dates and setting

Online via Prolific, January 17–28, 2022, ten weekday slots starting 2 pm GMT, plus a final continuation after slot ten.
January 17 to January 28, 2022PDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 4

Main data collection occurred online across ten weekday time slots; collection continued after the tenth slot to exceed 18,000 completions.

Number recruited and analyzed

NR for this design. Article reports 18,123 completed overall and about 400 per design; starts/randomized counts per design are not reported.
18,123 completed observations (about 400 per design)PDF page 2 · Introduction/results overview

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Two arms: competition and control.
one competition and one control conditionPDF page 2 · Introduction

Every design had a between-subject competition condition and control condition.

Unit of randomization

Four-participant batch assigned to one design-by-condition cell.
randomly redirected ... in batches of four participantsPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Batches of four participants, rather than single participants, were redirected to design-by-condition cells.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

Restricted balanced cycles: each sequence of 90 four-person batches assigns one batch to each of 45×2 cells; numerical marginal probabilities are implied but not stated. No stratification statement.
one batch per treatmentPDF page 8 · Materials and Methods, Data Collection and Randomization, item 3

Within each cycle of 90 batches, one four-person batch was randomly allocated to each of the 90 design-by-condition cells.

Exact treatment and comparator

Solve matrices for 5 minutes for £0.10 per self-reported correct answer, plus a £0.70 bonus for outperforming a randomly selected participant; control has the same per-answer payment without the competitive bonus.
difference between self-reported and actual performancePDF page 4 · Moderating Effect of Common Design Choices, ACH91 example

The article specifies the task, pay in both arms, competitive bonus, five-minute timing, and cheating outcome.

Outcome definitions and timing

Self-reported minus actual matrix performance, measured after the 5-minute task; labeled cheating/deception and used as the moral-behavior outcome.
difference between self-reported and actual performancePDF page 4 · Moderating Effect of Common Design Choices, ACH91 example

The article specifies the task, pay in both arms, competitive bonus, five-minute timing, and cheating outcome.

Competition-versus-control effect on the design's moral-behavior outcome, standardized as Cohen's d.
effect of competition on moral behaviorPDF page 2 · Results, Meta-Analytic Effect Size

The target per-design contrast is competition versus control on moral behavior, standardized to Cohen's d for synthesis.
